$schema_note: RetroForge ticket board. Fields: id, title, phase (roadmap phase), crate (primary write scope), write_scope (globs the executor may touch), depends_on (ticket ids), acceptance (ALL must pass before status=done), points (fibonacci), status (todo|in_progress|done|blocked), notes (OPTIONAL array of strings, append-only: HANDOFF:/BLOCKED: entries). ALWAYS-WRITABLE SET (in addition to write_scope, for every ticket): this file's own-ticket status+notes fields; docs/STATUS.md (append one line per merged ticket); Cargo.lock; docs/TECH_STACK.md section-2 rows (new-dependency decision record). Claim rule: a ticket is claimable when all depends_on are done. Executors: work ONE ticket per session, run `cargo fmt --check && cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings && cargo test --workspace && scripts/validate-arch.sh` plus ticket acceptance before marking done. Never widen write_scope beyond the always-writable set without a HANDOFF note in the ticket's notes array.

ROOT CAUSE 1 (PRIMARY, confirmed by inspection): crates/retroforge/src/core_thread.rs's loop sends CoreEvent::Frame from EXACTLY ONE place -- inside `if stepper.tick_running_with_input(...)`. That call returns false whenever the machine is Paused. StepFrame/StepScanline advance the emulator and render into `sink`, then force Paused, so the freshly rendered frame is computed and then silently DISCARDED, never sent. The machine really does step (state advances correctly); the user just never sees it. Verification: read the single send site; confirmed by the new headless test in acceptance criterion 2, which fails before the fix.

ROOT CAUSE 2 (COMPOUNDING, confirmed by inspection): crates/retroforge/src/app.rs's pump_core_events only calls ctx.request_repaint() when self.running. Even once root cause 1 is fixed, a stepped frame arrives over the channel a few ms AFTER the button click's own repaint has already completed, so with no repaint scheduled the frame would sit unconsumed until some unrelated event (a mouse move) happened to wake the UI. Fixing only root cause 1 would produce a maddening 'sometimes works if you jiggle the mouse' bug. Both must be fixed together.

NOT A BUG, recorded so it is not 'fixed' later: rf_renderer::FrameBuffer has no clear step -- video_scanline writes rows in place, so the buffer persists between frames. A scanline step therefore paints the new scanline over the previous frame's content, which is correct debugger behaviour; it also means a single scanline step is nearly imperceptible by design. Step Frame is the visible one.
